observations.summary: Per P25 this spec blocks on named missing capabilities, never on another spec's status. The three named capabilities are: live Red Alert publication (rlmarketaction.js rejects published === true with RLMKT-GATE and GATE.redAlertPublication is 'dependency-pending:feature-002'); a routable topic finding (supplied by Feature 019); and committed market data for the topics' instruments. Each has a specified degraded behaviour in spec.md, so none of them makes this spec blocked. specDependsOn names specs/019 as an artifact dependency for the finding contract, not as a status gate.

Several of the operator's own topics cannot produce a scoreable brief call today. loadInstrumentUniverse in scripts/recommendation-body.mjs builds the committed universe from data/bars/*.json, data/options/*.json and watchlist.json tickers. European defense listings, Brent, urea and potash are not in it. A swing or tactical call naming them resolves no-instrument-in-committed-universe and is withheld by scripts/validate-brief-payload.mjs, whose --drop-unscoreable path drops the offending claim and publishes the rest. Expanding the committed universe is Non-Goal 5 and is separate work. Certification must not treat 'a defense or fertilizer call published in nextSession.actions' as this feature's success signal.

FR-020-038 forbids modifying any destination threshold, cap, score, minimum or vocabulary. The concrete surfaces this protects are: the D16 swing/tactical evaluability rule and its direction-correct invalidation level requirement; config.thresholds.nextSessionMaxActions; the closed RLATTN-* refusal codes in rlattention.js including PRIVACY, DEEPLINK, VERB and OVERLAP; and red-alert-policy/v1 scoreThreshold 75, visibleCap 5, minSeverity 4, minIndependentOrigins 2, minOwnerEvidence 1. A topic origin buys no exemption from any of them. Any implementation that raises throughput by moving one of these numbers has failed the spec regardless of test results.

Where topic-action exclusions become reader-visible is undecided. The attention tier already has payload.attentionExclusions[] with code, field and reason, and the invariant that built plus excluded equals declared. The action list has no equivalent reader-visible channel today; scripts/validate-brief-payload.mjs withholds an unscoreable claim via --drop-unscoreable and reports to stderr. FR-020-037 requires a refused finding to remain visible to the operator, so design must resolve whether topic-action exclusions join an existing channel or need their own.

Whether routing injects an action directly or supplies material a lane may adopt is a write-disjointness question. scripts/brief-narrative-parallel.mjs gives each lane an exact set of owned top-level payload keys and permits it to write only .brief-work/<lane>.json, verified by readCompleteFragment against the declared key set. nextSession is authored upstream of the attention rebuild: scripts/brief-refresh-and-push.sh runs build-attention-items.mjs --recompose --write before validate-brief-payload.mjs. Design must place topic routing in that ordering without breaking lane write-disjointness.
